Bank Statement Import — MT940 / MultiCash

Imports SWIFT MT940 bank statements — the *.STA files of MultiCash, X-business and Business 24 — with VS/KS/SS, counterparty accounts and balances.

Version19.0.1.0.0
EditionCommunity and Enterprise
LicenceAGPL-3
Requiresaccount_statement_import_file, account_mt940_base, account_cz_bankfile_base

What it is for

Czech banks hand statements to accounting software as SWIFT MT940: MultiCash writes them as *.STA files (into MCCWIN in version 3.x, DATA in 4.x), and X-business and Business 24 use the same layout. The SWIFT part is the same everywhere; field :86: ("information to account owner") is not, and it is where the variable, constant and specific symbols, the counterparty's account and name and the payment message live.

This module imports such files through the OCA statement import wizard (account_statement_import_file), on Community and Enterprise alike. It is the statement half of MultiCash; the payment half is account_multicash.

What is read

Field Becomes
:25: account the journal the statement belongs to
:28C: statement number the statement name MT940 <account>/<number>
:60F: / :60M: opening balance the statement's opening balance and its currency
:61: transaction a statement line: amount, sign (C credit, D debit, RC/RD reversals), booking date (else the value date), SWIFT transaction type, customer reference
:86: details label, VS/KS/SS, counterparty account and name
:62F: / :62M: closing balance the statement's closing balance

The :86: field. Banks write it as ?NN subfields and do not agree on the numbering — Česká spořitelna puts KS: in ?20 and VS: in ?21, Raiffeisenbank puts KS in ?21 and VS in ?22. The module therefore recognises a symbol by its prefix (VS, KS, SS, with or without a colon, zero-padded or not), never by its position. The counterparty comes from ?30 (bank code or BIC), ?31 (account), ?38 (IBAN) and ?32/?33 (name); the message from ?00, ?20–?29 and ?60–?63. Recurring noise such as Raiffeisenbank's statement number and zero fee lines is dropped. A :86: without subfields is kept as free text, and VS:-style tokens are still picked out of it.

On each statement line:

  • Label: counterparty name, message, VS:…, KS:…, SS:…, counterparty account.
  • Partner: looked up from the counterparty account among the bank accounts in Odoo.
  • Symbols: with l10n_cssk_payment_symbols installed, also in the line's own symbol fields.
  • The raw :61:/:86: text is kept on the line, the customer reference goes to Reference, the SWIFT type to Transaction Type.

One file may hold several days and several accounts; each statement lands on its own journal. A statement split over several messages (:60M: opening, same statement number, opening equal to the previous closing) is joined into one.

The file is read as UTF-8 if it is valid UTF-8, otherwise as code page 852 or Windows-1250, whichever yields more Czech letters.

Setting it up

  • Every account in the file needs a bank journal with that bank account (Accounting → Configuration → Accounting → Journals), in the statement's currency.
  • The account can be written either way. Česká spořitelna writes :25: as 0800/192000145399 (bank code first), others as an IBAN. The module compares bank code, prefix and number, so a journal whose account is stored as a CZ IBAN or as 19-2000145399/0800 is found in both cases.

Importing a statement

Accounting → Accounting → Import Statement, or Import Statement (OCA) on the bank journal's card in the Accounting dashboard. Choose the .STA file and press Import and View.

Importing the same statement again is refused line by line: each line's import key is made from the account, the statement number, the value date, the line's position on the statement, the amount and the bank reference. A file overlapping an earlier import brings in only the new lines.

Limitations

  • The :86: layout was checked against the published descriptions of Česká spořitelna (MultiCash 3.2, also valid for Business 24) and Raiffeisenbank (MT940 versions 2–4 for MultiCash and X-business). Other banks' MT940 is read through the same SWIFT fields, but their :86: has not been compared with a published layout; with free-text :86: the label is the text as given.
  • Matching the journal by bank code, prefix and number works for Czech and Slovak accounts. A foreign account must match the journal's account as written.
  • The import key includes the line's position on the statement. If a bank re-issues a statement with the lines in a different order, lines may be imported twice.
  • MT940 has two-digit years; dates are read as 1980–2079.
